en.headline: Hand, foot and mouth disease activity rises sharply in schools
en.dek: The Centre for Health Protection recorded nine institutional outbreaks involving 24 people in the first three days of the week, with about 90 per cent in child-care centres, kindergartens or primary schools.
body: Hand, foot and mouth disease activity has risen sharply in Hong Kong, the Centre for Health Protection said, with institutional outbreaks climbing from eight in mid-September to 20 last week involving 48 people.

In the first three days of this week the centre logged nine outbreaks involving 24 people. About nine-tenths of the recent clusters have been in child-care centres, kindergartens or primary schools. Sentinel surveillance at those settings also showed a marked jump in activity.

University of Hong Kong paediatric professor Patrick Ip said on a radio programme this morning that the increase became more noticeable from early October as the school term progressed. He reminded parents that alcohol does not effectively kill the enteroviruses involved and that children should wash with soap for at least 20 seconds. The centre has written to schools urging them to monitor the situation and report clusters promptly.

zh.headline: 手足口病活躍程度顯著上升 本周首三日已錄9宗爆發
zh.dek: 衞生防護中心指涉及24人，約九成發生在幼兒中心、幼稚園或小學，專家提醒用梘液洗手至少20秒。
body: 本港手足口病活躍程度近日顯著上升。衞生署衞生防護中心表示，院舍及學校爆發個案由9月中一周的8宗（涉及27人），增至上周的20宗（涉及48人）。
本周首三日已錄得9宗爆發個案，涉及24人，當中約九成發生在幼兒中心、幼稚園或小學。幼兒中心及幼稚園的定點監測數據亦顯示過去一周活動明顯增加。
港大醫學院兒童及青少年科學系臨床教授葉柏強今早在電台節目表示，自10月初學期展開後，爆發情況更為顯著。他提醒酒精未能有效殺滅相關腸病毒，學童應用梘液清潔雙手至少20秒。防護中心已向學校發信，呼籲留意最新情況並盡快呈報爆發個案。
